papers.title: Whaler's note
lines: Grytviken: a harbour, a church, a factory, and a smell I will take to my grave.
They say the whales are gone. They are not gone, they are in the water, and they are listening.

papers.title: Seal-counter's note
lines: Counted three hundred elephant seals on the beach, none of them in a good mood.
Retreated to the hut. The one who followed has opinions and a very large nose.

papers.title: Visitor's note
lines: At the whalers' cemetery we raised a glass to the explorer buried there, and poured a little on the grave.
It is the tradition. The wind took the rest.

papers.title: Rat-eradication note
lines: South Georgia was declared rat-free after years of work by people and dogs and helicopters.
The pipits came back to the island, and now they sing at breakfast.
